title: Building a Balanced Plate
hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.
key_points: Fill half your plate with fruits and vegetables — more color and variety is better.
Make about a quarter whole grains, like brown rice, oats, or whole-wheat bread, over refined ones.
Reserve a quarter for protein: beans, fish, poultry, eggs, nuts, or lean meat.
Make water your default drink and keep added sugar, sodium, and saturated fat low.
content_html: Healthy eating sounds complicated until you picture a single plate. MyPlate, the U.S. government's eating guide, turns the dietary guidelines into one image: half your plate fruits and vegetables, a quarter whole grains, and a quarter protein, with a side of dairy or a dairy alternative.
extra_html: According to the USDA's MyPlate guidance, the goal isn't a rigid diet but a flexible pattern you can apply to almost any meal. Vegetables and fruit take up the biggest share because they're rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals for relatively few calories. Choosing whole grains over refined ones keeps more of that fiber, and varying your proteins — including plant sources like beans and nuts — covers your needs without leaning only on red meat. The guidance also nudges you to make water your go-to drink and to limit the three things most of us get too much of: added sugars, sodium, and saturated fat. It's a starting frame, not a calorie ledger — useful precisely because you can eyeball it.

related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.hook: The official protein guideline is a floor set to prevent deficiency — not the amount that keeps you strong. A new review argues most people, especially with age, do better with more.

flashcards.prompt: Roughly how much of your plate should be fruits and vegetables?
flashcards.back_html: About half. The other half splits between whole grains (a quarter) and protein (a quarter).

flashcards.prompt: Which grain choice fits the MyPlate guidance best?

choices.text: Whole grains like brown rice or oats

flashcards.explanation_html: MyPlate recommends making at least half your grains whole grains — they keep more fiber and nutrients than refined grains.

flashcards.prompt: What does MyPlate suggest as your default drink?
flashcards.back_html: Water. It keeps you hydrated without the added sugar and calories of soda or juice.
